title: W4 export branch isolation — query runs THROUGH BranchScope, no withoutGlobalScope, client branch_id is additive-only
proof: OrderHistoryExport::collection() (line 46) calls $this->orderService->list($request). OrderService::list (OrderService.php:135) starts from Order::with([...])->where(...) — a plain Eloquent query on the Order model. Order::booted (app/Models/Order.php:129) calls static::addGlobalScope(new BranchScope()); so BranchScope is applied automatically. grep 'withoutGlobalScope' app/Services/OrderService.php => only hits at 2559/2572 (an unrelated User lookup), NOT in list(). branch_id IS present in $orderFilter (OrderService.php:73), so a client may pass ?branch_id=X, but BranchScope::apply (app/Models/Scopes/BranchScope.php:38) ANDs a staff WHERE branch_id = userBranch on top: a branch operator passing branch_id=2 yields WHERE branch_id=userBranch AND branch_id=2 => empty set, NOT a cross-branch read. Admin (branch_id=0) gets no scope filter (BranchScope.php:33-35) and may filter to any branch — that is the intended admin-sees-all behavior. The export reuses the SAME scoped path as the proven index() endpoint.
reproduction: git show b95dac18a:app/Exports/OrderHistoryExport.php; sed -n '125,235p' app/Services/OrderService.php; grep -n 'addGlobalScope' app/Models/Order.php (=> line 129); sed -n '17,45p' app/Models/Scopes/BranchScope.php
remediation: None. No scope bypass mechanism present. Latent cloud note: branch_id being a client-passable filter is harmless under BranchScope, but a V2 SaaS hardening pass could whitelist branch_id to admin-only at the request layer for defense-in-depth.

title: W4 export authz — route is inside auth:sanctum group AND has the same inline pos-orders|pos gate as index/show; Chef role is meaningfully blocked
proof: ROUTE LAYER: the export route (routes/api.php:976) sits inside the admin prefix group declared at routes/api.php:295 with middleware ['installed','apiKey','auth:sanctum','block_kiosk_token_admin','localization','throttle:admin-mutation'] (brace-tracking confirms the group spans lines 295-1253, enclosing 976). EMPIRICAL: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8769/api/admin/order-history/export returns HTTP 302 -> /api/login with Content-Type text/html (auth:sanctum redirect), NOT a 200 SPA-catchall masquerade and NOT a 200 XLSX — so the route is genuinely wired behind auth. CONTROLLER LAYER: export() (OrderHistoryController.php:80-83) runs abort_unless(auth()->user()?->can('pos-orders') || auth()->user()?->can('pos'), 403), byte-identical to the already-proven index()/show() gates (lines 49-53 / 102-106). EFFECTIVENESS: database/seeders/RolePermissionTableSeeder.php — Branch Manager (line 16-17) and POS Operator (line 86-87) hold pos+pos-orders; CHEF (lines 115-119) holds ONLY ['dashboard','kitchen-display-system','order-status-screen'] => an authenticated Chef is BLOCKED by the gate. The gate is meaningful, not just defense-in-depth.
reproduction: curl -s -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://127.0.0.1:8769/api/admin/order-history/export (=> 302 text/html, redirect to /api/login); sed -n '295p;972,980p' routes/api.php; sed -n '80,93p' app/Http/Controllers/Admin/OrderHistoryController.php; awk '/EnumRole::CHEF/,/chefPermissionNames\)/' database/seeders/RolePermissionTableSeeder.php
remediation: None. SUSPECTED (not reproduced by me): the AUTHENTICATED positive path (admin login -> GET export -> 200 + real XLSX). The W4 commit message asserts '200 + real XLSX, date-filtered' but as the adversary I did not mint an admin session, so I do not relay that as confirmed. Orchestrator to reproduce: Playwright login admin@lecayenne.fr on :8769 (read flow, allowed) then GET /api/admin/order-history/export and assert 200 + xlsx content-type + Historique.xlsx + correct columns; ALSO mint a Chef token and assert 403.

title: W1 receipt label lowercasing — defensive NO-OP (keys already lowercase literals), cannot break existing labels or leak raw labels; receipt comps NOT frozen

The builder pushes ONLY three literal keys, all already lowercase: 'fiscal_ticket_no' (116), 'audit_fingerprint' (119), 'legal_mentions' (122). Both receipt components consume the SAME builder.
